analysis: The closest option directly develops media interpretation across formats and periods, public rhetoric and persuasion, empirical methods, environmental messaging and public documentary and podcast work. Political and social courses contextualise the global questions. The research methods give genuine partial coverage but do not reproduce a dedicated comparative content analysis sequence, communication project or placement.

The second option has the same empirical and media foundation, but its differentiating venture, product development, market research, international business and leadership courses make organisational audience decisions and research a sustained purpose. Marketing and persuasion in both options reinforce the comparability without erasing the difference.

alignment.rationale: Both examine changes in media and their social consequences. UCR follows American media and storytelling; UvA compares global digital production, algorithms, privacy and regulation.
No selected UCR course directly covers the specific UvA Communication Theme 2: Crises & Resilience requirement at its stated scope and credit weight; this distinct component remains visible.
UCR media and social psychology courses contribute to parts of the subject. No single selected course covers comparative communication-science theories across societies.
Both introduce research designs, data collection and statistical inference. UCR applies these skills in a general research project; UvA uses communication-science examples and SPSS.
Both develop experimental reasoning and analysis of human behaviour. UCR emphasises experimental design and statistical models; UvA also has students conduct a communication survey.
Both teach qualitative research design, interviews, focus groups and interpretation. UCR also covers ethnography and visual methods, while UvA focuses on intercultural communication research.

academicConstruction: Rhetoric in Action is unavailable in term four. Swap it with Market Research from term six. The venture prerequisite remains in term three and research methods are already completed. The programmes retain six and seven advanced units and 180 EC. Reviewed the third direction using direct climate communication, Media & the Environment and Persuasive Communication, then health psychology, health evidence and sustainability context. The issue content does not create a cumulative sequence in health messaging, intercultural health communication or campaign evaluation. This is an academic coherence decision.
